commits.message:
Verify authenticated event-history delivery checkpoints

Add absent-ID, honest-challenge refusal and combined maximum-shape acceptance fixtures. Verify the actual production owner at the proposed retention profile, preserve measurement provenance, and record the remaining live prerequisites. Local checkpoints 1–3 pass; the prepared live campaign remains blocked before deployment. Full protocol acceptance and deferred recovery remain open.

Integrate authenticated event-history delivery checkpoint

Consolidate the contract, SDK, proof, watcher and production-owner work with
the completed cleanup in the original checkout. Preserve authenticated sorted
UTxO history, signed intent, retained membership and the bounded dependent
rollback repair; document the remaining acceptance gates.

Verified production deposit/withdrawal journeys, current observed recovery,
required node (125) and emulator (64) cases, 195 Aiken history tests, 13 installed
transition lifecycle cases, and 1,340 independently decoded signed receipts.
Regenerate the transition fit ledger with prior evidence retained locally.

This is an integration checkpoint, not full acceptance or an ABI freeze.
Reference-input fixture, broader recovery/crash coverage, remaining proof/ABI
acceptance, existing-state migration and live deployment gates remain open.
See docs/fault-proofs/event-history-delivery-checkpoint.md for scope and evidence.

Fix pre-push review findings and apply the skipped format and lint pass

- Node CI: the compose render step copies .env.example to .env, since
  every node stack requires an operator .env beside it and a fresh checkout
  has none; the step failed on every run.
- Node retention: test that a terminal transition shallower than the
  manifest's finality depth is refused, the only database-side guard
  before a removed header's payload becomes prunable.
- Watcher: drop two comments describing the deleted node admin key.
- Run the prettier and eslint pass the pre-commit hook would have run on
  the preceding commits (import order, one test fixture); keep the
  committee's late-assigned interval and API server as let, since the tick
  runner's fatal exit closes over them before they exist.

Rename the DA watcher to the committee node, coordinate locally, and bound DA retention

Rename the da-committee-node's watcher service and stores to committee
terms (committee-service.ts, CommitteeStore, the "committee" DA transport
target and libp2p runtime manifest host) across the node, core, node-tools
and docs.

Make the operator launch path work from a fresh clone:
- delete the never-executed l1-services compose; the midgard-node Kupmios
  overlay is the L1 stack, with Kupo pinned by digest and run without
  --prune-utxo, one cardano-node default, and the mithril client moved to
  its maintained image;
- delete the dead node .dockerignore and da-libp2p overlay, fix the
  benchmark overlay, interpolate PORT in ports and healthchecks;
- render every node compose combination and the phase-4 devnet compose in
  node CI, build the node image and smoke its CLI; install pnpm from each
  package.json in the docs-site and pages workflows;
- point the docs-site L1 backend, local stack and committee pages at the
  overlay and drop the removed release-evidence digest gate.

State-queue mutation coordination (D8):
- The watcher and fault-proof removal paths use one local retry-until-
  confirmed coordinator; the node URL, admin key and lease TTL leave the
  watcher process config, the fault-proof CLI flags and the journey harness
  lease server. A journal recorded under a node-URL source is refused.
- The node's HTTP state-queue mutation lease endpoint, its resolver, routes
  and tests are deleted; the internal lease and its status field stay.

Watcher startup (D11): the readiness header hash is a fixed constant and
journals live under readiness/<category> and bindings/<category>.

Watcher packaging (D9): watcher-process.example.json and
authority.example.json templates with parse tests, .env.example, a
two-service compose (authority + watcher) rendered in CI with the pinned
image check, and a README section for running it.

DA retention (D7): one core prune decision (confirmed head and live queue
retain, removed or past the required window prunes, otherwise retain) is
shared by the node and the committee. Both read the confirmed head and live
queue from authenticated L1 only, retry while the view is unavailable and
exit once L1_VIEW_FATAL_MS passes. RETENTION_DAYS=0 no longer disables
payload pruning; the node prunes in one DELETE; the SDK retention-evidence
module and the committee's availability retention source are deleted.

Add authenticated event history and the completed-fraud queue marker (in progress)

Work in progress from the event-history program; ABI not frozen and no gap
closure claimed. See docs/fault-proofs/event-history-progress.md.

- Aiken: event-history library (admission, funding, horizon, mutation,
  ordering, output claims, proof evidence, retained data, retirement) and
  the user-events history, history-data and history-retirement validators;
  fabricated-deposit and fabricated-withdrawal steps 01-04 read the paired
  history; state-queue nodes carry a proven_fraud marker.
- SDK: event-history capture, funding, payload, proof, query and build
  helpers; fabricated-family contracts take history parameters.
- Fault proofs: fabricated history witness, completed-fraud and proof
  validity modules; fabricated-family preparation and submission read the
  history; emulator coverage for capture, list, output claims, retention,
  preparation and the completed-fraud marker.
- Core, node and watcher fixtures: deployment identity requires
  event-history bounds; manifests, contract registration and merge readiness
  follow the proven_fraud marker.

Known incomplete: the watcher's createCatalogueCompleteCanonicalReplay call
does not yet pass the new history input.

Pin Ogmios v7.0.0 and cardano-node 11.1.0 at every L1 stack site

The three L1 stacks disagreed: l1-services ran Ogmios v6.11.0 against
cardano-node 10.6.3, the kupmios compose defaulted Ogmios to the floating
`latest` tag next to node 11.0.1, and only the devnet pinned v7.0.0 by
digest with node 11.1.0. All three now use the devnet's digests.

- l1-services: Ogmios v7.0.0 by digest; the node image example moves to
  11.1.0 by digest, which is what v7.0.0 is built against.
- kupmios compose and env example: the Ogmios default is the digest-pinned
  v7.0.0 tag instead of `latest`. The node tag stays a plain `11.1.0`
  because the Mithril bootstrap script parses it as a version to compare
  against the certified snapshot's node version.
- Docs table and the local L1 observation helper's fidelity note updated
  to match. The v6 to v7 transaction schema change only drops empty
  `validityInterval` and `outputs`; the shapes the helper asserts are
  unchanged, and the renamed reference-script parameter is already
  normalised by the manifest reader and the pinned Kupmios provider.

Single-source the classifier's replay requirements and gate on the predecessor ledger

The header classifier carried three literal category lists: the families
whose fault proof opens prev_utxos_root and therefore need the
authenticated predecessor ledger, and (twice) the families whose
detection replays the historical native-script corpus. The watcher
kept its own copy of the first list and gated fault decisions on
`replayContext === undefined`. That gate was vacuous in production:
the launch scope always includes crossBlockDuplicateEvent, whose
settlement capture attaches a context to every decision, so a
predecessor-family decision that omitted the predecessor passed.

Both sets now live in workflow/replay-requirements.ts as
PREDECESSOR_LEDGER_PROOF_CATEGORIES and
HISTORICAL_CORPUS_REPLAY_CATEGORIES with a `launchScopeRequires`
helper; the classifier and the watcher derive from them. The doc
comments record that these are not the registry's `requires` sets:
`replayContext` there means the artifact re-derives from the admitted
context object, which is a different fact enforced at load time.

The watcher's decision-time gate now checks the invariant the
classifier actually establishes: a fault decision in a predecessor
family on a header that commits a non-empty previous ledger must carry
`replayContext.predecessor`. A genesis-ledger header is admitted
without one. Families that only need the context object are admitted
at decision time and refused by their application record at load,
which the tests pin per family. Disabling the gate fails exactly the
eight refusal cases.

New tests pin both sets against the catalogue and the registry: the
corpus set is a strict subset of the historicalNativeScriptAuthority
families, and the ledger set intersects the registry's replayContext
families in exactly noReferenceInput and nonExistentInput.

Closes #677.

Speed up the watcher and fault-proof test suites

The fault-proof suite drops from about 43 to about 20 minutes at eight
forks and the watcher suite from about 26 minutes at two forks to about
four at eight, with every test still isolated per file. The savings come
from removing repeated work rather than from adding forks:

- core validation-merkle: memoize the membership index per leaf array so
  proofs for a 1,304-asset value no longer rebuild the frontier per leaf.
- sdk blueprint: apply blueprint parameters with the aiken uplc wasm
  applier (byte-identical to the JavaScript applier over every
  parameterised validator, roughly ten times faster) and key the applied
  script cache by the raw inputs instead of hashing the compiled code on
  every lookup. Adds @lucid-evolution/uplc as a direct sdk dependency at
  the pin lucid already uses.
- fault-proofs journal: fold the workflow incrementally instead of
  revalidating the whole journal on every append and load.
- fault-proofs runtime: memoize the seed-derived signer per Lucid
  instance instead of re-deriving the BIP32 key on every step.
- mint-authorization: index the batch generator by encoded state instead
  of replaying from the first batch on every evaluate step, and memoize
  artifact admission by digest.
- transition-trace: memoize the MPF trie per root object.
- watcher catalogue fixture: emit definite-length CBOR for positional
  script bytes; the indefinite heads made cbor-x decode pathologically.
- watcher user-event-history test: compare byte stores by content rather
  than through deep equality on large typed arrays.
- watcher vitest: derive the fork count from the host with an override
  through MIDGARD_WATCHER_FORKS.
- fault-proofs vitest: rank the longest emulator files first on cold
  runs, record the measured suite shape, and pick the evaluator per
  harness. Scalus stays the default for mint authorization because two
  size-at-maximum cases pass under it while the aiken evaluator reports
  them a few thousand memory units over the limit; that disagreement is
  an open question and is documented at the harness option. Lifecycles
  away from the limit opt into the faster aiken evaluator.

Document that the retained-DA transport starts locally and is not retried in process

The shared retained-DA transport does not dial a peer when it starts: it
builds the local libp2p node with inbound gated and no listen address, and
peers are dialed per retrieval request under a lease. A start failure is
therefore local and deterministic. The classification that first needs the
transport fails closed, the process exits 70 with the error in its
failed_closed record, and a restart owns a fresh transport, so the sticky
failed status needs no in-process retry with backoff.

Say so in the owner's status comment, the README readiness section, and the
challenger runbook, and name the two tests after the start failure they
exercise instead of a dial.

Test the watcher's decision-time predecessor-authority gate per family

The gate in the fault-proof application's classifyHeader entry refuses a
fault decision for a family whose record requires the predecessor replay
context when the classifier retained none. Until now only the set was
pinned; the check itself, its refusal, and what the runner later sees were
untested for the three families #675 widened it to. The new table-driven
test drives the real entry with the classifier module as a double: every
predecessor family is refused at the exact message and leaves no replay
context for its runner, whose record then refuses at its own requires
gate; every predecessor family with a retained context is admitted and the
loader hands that context to the record, which resolves exactly its
roster; every other installed family is admitted without one. Disabling
the gate fails exactly the five refusal cases.

Report the shared retained-DA transport in operations status

Startup readiness stopped opening the retained-DA transport in #675, so
its health needs a live home. The retained-DA runtime owner now exposes
the state of its one shared transport (idle until the first workflow
launch, opening, open, failed with the dial error, closed); the fault-proof
application delegates to it and operations status carries it, adding the
retained_da_transport_failed readiness reason when a dial has failed.
Closing an owner whose dial failed no longer re-throws the dial error.
The watcher README states what startup readiness proves versus what
operations status reports.

Re-measure the transition-trace workflow fit ledger against the current blueprint

The committed ledger was bound to blueprint 11593a4e; the installed
lifecycle test re-derives it from the blueprint in use and has rewritten it
in every session since. Same 486 entries, re-measured against 04790ae6
under the same compiler.

Add the authenticated event-history architecture proposal for NIFP-01 to 03

A design document proposing a cumulative authenticated event dictionary
with deterministic shards and immutable checkpoints, its security
properties, alternatives, retention, batched-admission fallback, cost
model and acceptance criteria, plus a research note recording the current
fabricated-event, watcher retention and transition-trace boundaries it
starts from. Status is Proposed; remaining-gaps.md now points at it and
records that the gaps stay open until it is accepted and implemented.

Drop the prose facts and voice checks and enforce lint and format in CI

The docs-site facts check restated source inventories in a script and the
voice check pattern-matched wording; both went red on ordinary source drift
without proving a documentation claim, and their trigger lists had to
mirror every source they read. They are removed with their CI steps and
path triggers; the link check stays. The documentation policy and the
catalogue-status table now say plainly that prose counts are verified by
reading the source. The demo workspace lint and format-check that the
pre-commit hook applies locally are now enforced in midgard-node-ci.yml,
which the hook's header cites instead of the retired gate names. The cg1
control-publication gate no longer verifies the exclusion's prose citation
against the necessity memo; the exclusion itself is still checked for
genuine absence and for being a real role.

Verify the family registry program against its baseline and review the glossary (#676)

Full fault-proofs and watcher suites re-run once against a fresh blueprint
(byte-identical to the one on disk) and reconciled with the ticket-1
baseline; the watcher journey suite and node-tools typecheck are green.
The glossary entries for the family application registry and the family
record are reviewed against the landed code: the allow-list is gone, the
registry's key set is the installed set, a record carries the
decision-digest flag and refuses a missing required part unless a
reconciliation-only permit is held, and hand-written rows declare their
type arguments.
